prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a modular 2D animation rig sprite sheet for the four adult beach volleyball athletes in the reference. These are non-graphic paper-doll game art components for skeletal animation, NOT injured people. Preserve the exact faces, hair accessories, uniforms and shaded arcade pixel-art style.
EXACT 6 columns x4 rows, 1536x1024 transparent PNG. Each256px square cell contains a single isolated sprite component. No background, glow, shadows, labels or grid. Empty space true alpha0.
Row1 red male brown headband; row2 red female brown ponytail hibiscus; row3 blue male blond sunglasses; row4 blue female dark ponytail visor. All characters face RIGHT in consistent side/three-quarter view.
COLUMNS identical for all rows:
1 HEAD+TORSO+PELVIS with entire hair and uniform shorts, but NO arms and NO legs. Arms removed cleanly at shoulder; legs removed at shorts openings. Head near top24, shorts endy232. Neutral torso, slight running forward lean, facing right, no body rotation. This is the central paper-doll component.
2 isolated UPPER ARM, straight vertical from round shoulder at y40 to elbow at y216. Natural skin shading, no hand. Joint ends softly rounded for overlap.
3 isolated FOREARM + CLOSED FIST + team wristband, vertical elbow at y40 to wrist/fist at y216. Natural skin shading.
4 isolated UPPER LEG/THIGH, vertical hip at y40 to knee at y216. Bare athletic thigh, natural skin shading, rounded joint ends, no lower leg. Shorts stay in column1.
5 isolated LOWER LEG/SHIN, vertical knee at y40 to ankle at y216, natural shin and calf shading, no foot.
6 isolated bare FOOT in right-facing side profile, heel on left and toes on right, horizontal, ankle attachment visible at x100,y150. Entire foot centered with ample padding.
Each part should have sharp dark outline, warm highlights and shadows matching the reference, solid opaque interiors and genuinely transparent outside. These six parts will be joined by code at shoulders, elbows, hips, knees and ankles to guarantee continuous right/left limb motion. Keep the parts separate and complete, each in its own exact cell. No full-body figures, no duplicate parts inside a cell.
note: Final frames are baked by the Canvas rig with fixed anatomical limb identities and ordered gait phases.
